mocks.name: MOCK-02-001
mocks.reason: Fake computed boundary-source provider standing in for S3's real useTokenBoundaries computed branch, so AC-UX-2/AC-UX-3/AC-UX-4/AC-UX-8/AC-ERR-1 are verifiable against a computed source without a live tokenizer. Injected only in tests/unit/token-view.test.tsx's rendering-contract suite; chat-workspace.tsx's production call site passes no computedSource.

implementation_notes: src/lib/token-view.ts owns (AC-STRUCT-3): SEPARATOR (U+2502)/NEWLINE_MARKER (U+21B5)/SPACE_RUN_MARKER (U+00B7) constants, resolveBoundarySource (pure), useTokenBoundaries (hook: stream branch reads step.contentTokens live every render with no id-keyed cache, per the S1 carry-forward invariant that the array can grow under a stable step id; computed branch keys pending/resolved state on (step.id, step.content) with stale-response cancellation guarding), formatTokenViewText (single character-level pass building one display string), and getBoundaryNotice (label/caveat text, null for pending). chat-workspace.tsx's new TokenViewStepContent component only calls these exports — no inline regex/substitution logic for ↵/·/│ in chat-workspace.tsx (VQ-S2-002).

IMPLEMENTATION DECISION (AC-UX-4 space-run wording, flagged as VQ-S2-014, not escalated): 'Each space in a run of two or more MUST render as one ·' is genuinely ambiguous between collapsing the whole run to one glyph vs. replacing each space in the run 1:1. Chose 1:1 replacement (a 3-space run → three ·) — preserves visual column alignment and matches the common 'show whitespace' editor convention; pinned by a dedicated 3-space-run test. If the spec author intended the collapse reading, it's a one-line change confined to formatTokenViewText's loop with no ripple elsewhere.

IMPLEMENTATION DECISION (AC-UX-1 'switch' wording): implemented as a Checkbox+FormControlLabel ('Show tokens'), not MUI's Switch component, for consistency with every other boolean sidebar toggle in chat-workspace.tsx (renderMarkdown, showExamples, showTour, hideSystemPrompt, four collapse-by-default toggles) — all use Checkbox. MUI Switch renders role="switch" rather than role="checkbox", which would both break this story's own role-based test queries and introduce a new, inconsistent toggle-control convention into the file.

S1 carry-forward item 1 (S1-F8, compactSteps drops whitespace-only assistant steps, server/ollama-client.ts:240-241): confirmed this is a real, constructible AC-UX-4 gap — a completion whose entire content is whitespace (e.g. a model response of just \"\\n\\n\") is silently dropped server-side before it ever reaches the client, so AC-UX-4's newline-marker guarantee is unreachable via live streaming for such a step; only a directly-seeded/persisted step (as this story's own tests use) can exercise it. Not fixed — pre-existing, out of S2's scope per the story brief. Left for the epic owner/BACKLOG to judge whether it's worth a fix.

S1 carry-forward item 2 (contentTokens growth under a stable step id): useTokenBoundaries's stream branch never caches by step.id alone — it reads step.contentTokens directly off the step object on every render, so applyDelta's shallow-spread streaming (chat-workspace.tsx) is reflected immediately. Pinned by a dedicated renderHook test that grows contentTokens under the same step id across a rerender and asserts the returned tokens array updates.

S1 carry-forward item 3 (ConversationStep duplication): confirmed S2 adds no new fields to ConversationStep in either server/types.ts or src/types/chat.ts. Boundary source is a purely derived concept living entirely in src/lib/token-view.ts, never persisted.

S1 carry-forward item 4 (S1-F9, silent quota-retry failure, AC-ERR-4 gap): judged OUT OF SCOPE for S2, not silently absorbed and not silently fixed. AC-ERR-1's notice mechanism is specifically about a step's token-boundary source (attached to one step's rendered content); a persistence-failure signal is an app-level concern with no single step to attach a notice to, so reusing AC-ERR-1's surface for it would conflate two unrelated concerns rather than genuinely reuse a fitting mechanism. Recording this call for the curator/BACKLOG rather than expanding S2's scope to build a new notice surface unprompted. S1-F9 remains open in ownership-ledger.json.

Delegated the token-view.ts fill-in and chat-workspace.tsx wiring to a base:dev spawn against a fully-specified algorithm and the two pre-written TDD test files (tests/unit/token-view.test.tsx, tests/unit/chat-workspace-token-view.test.tsx). Verified the dev's diff directly (git diff) rather than trusting its summary: token-view.ts's five function bodies match the given algorithm exactly with no signature/constant drift; chat-workspace.tsx's diff is confined to the specified sidebar-state/checkbox/render-branch/TokenViewStepContent additions with no unrelated changes. Dev also made three legitimate fixture-only fixes to its own test file (none weakened an assertion): seedConversation needed a synthetic user step because chat-workspace.tsx's pre-existing visibleConversations filter hides any conversation lacking one; the reload-scenario helper needed to become idempotent for AC-UX-1's second call; AC-UX-7's innerHTML baseline snapshot needed to be captured after opening the Client section rather than before, since expanding the right sidebar independently reflows the transcript's max-width (a pre-existing, unrelated layout rule) that would otherwise fail the round-trip comparison regardless of token-view correctness.

POST-DELEGATION FIX (found during my own independent Regression Prevention pass, not by dev): tests/unit/chat-workspace-token-view.test.tsx as delivered did not explicitly `import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, vi } from \"vitest\"`, relying on globals — this reproduced the same systemic 'missing vitest/globals types' tsc gap documented in architecture.md's pre-existing-red-state section (201 errors across 4 files), adding 48 NEW errors (249 total) purely from this one new file. S1's own new unit test file (tests/unit/chat-content-tokens-quota.test.ts) had already established the clean workaround — an explicit vitest import — but nothing in architecture.md's documented red-state section states this as a required pattern for new files; it's only discoverable by diffing S1's file against the baseline-red ones. Added the explicit import; typecheck confirmed back to exactly 201 (zero net new).

verification_summary.tsc_frontend: 201 pre-existing errors (4 files), matches Step 0 baseline exactly (measured with --incremental false); 0 net new after fixing the vitest-import gap in the new wiring test file
verification_summary.test_unit: 83 passed / 1 failed (baseline 50/1; +33 new, all passing; the 1 failure is the pre-existing out-of-scope chat-workspace.test.tsx:175 button-label mismatch, unchanged)
verification_summary.test_integration: 27 passed / 0 failed (baseline 27/0; +0 new — story is frontend-only, integration suite unaffected as expected)

retrospective.harder_than_needed: AC-UX-4's space-run wording ('Each space in a run of two or more MUST render as one ·') is genuinely ambiguous between collapsing a whole run to one glyph and replacing each space in the run 1:1 — the AC's own grammar reads as evidence for 1:1 replacement, while the pre-impl VQ-S2-010's parenthetical ('one · per run') reads as evidence for the collapse reading, and no spec.md Design Decision resolves it. Had to reason this out and pin the choice with an explicit test plus a post-impl verification question rather than follow an unambiguous rule. Separately, the established convention that new tests/unit/*.tsx files must explicitly import test globals from \"vitest\" to avoid this repo's pre-existing systemic tsc gap is only discoverable by diffing S1's own clean test file against the four baseline-red files — architecture.md's documented pre-existing-red-state section describes the gap but not the workaround, so a fresh test file (including the dev's first draft here) can silently reproduce the same error class and only get caught by an independent post-hoc typecheck diff.
retrospective.surprised_by: chat-workspace.tsx's visibleConversations filter silently hides any seeded conversation lacking a `kind: \"user\"` step — unrelated to token-view's own contract, but it silently broke every fixture in the wiring test suite (nothing was ever findable in the DOM) until diagnosed.

absorbed_from.note: Found and fixed three test-fixture-only bugs unrelated to token-view's own logic: (1) seedConversation needed a synthetic user step to satisfy visibleConversations' filter; (2) the Client-section-opening test helper needed to become idempotent for AC-UX-1's post-reload second call; (3) AC-UX-7's innerHTML baseline snapshot needed to be captured after opening the Client section (not before), since expanding the right sidebar independently reflows the transcript's max-width.
